beats.text: Aria has been asking about the strange leaves all week — "but what IS it?" Tonight, an answer. Fireside lesson: Owen passes around tall stalks with hand-shaped leaves and thick pale roots. Someone asks a dumb question. Nobody minds. That's how you learn.
👁 It whistles when it clocks you — and the whole meadow hears it. Wind it before it reaches the burrow, or hunt the whistlers last.
★ IDENTIFIED: Jerusalem Artichoke. Tall sunflower stalks; dig at the base for knobby tubers. Uses unknown — harvest, taste, and learn.

💡 You see it again in your mind: tall sunflower-like stalks with knobby tubers at the base, found in sunny patches. your teacher's words land on the memory like a label. Jerusalem Artichoke. Of course.
★ IDENTIFIED: Sweet Manioc. Manioc. Tall stalks, hand-shaped leaves, thick roots. Uses unknown — harvest, taste, and learn.
📖 LEARNED: Stalk (Level 2). Distance closes without permission.
🌟 JACKPOT: A stranger by the road knows things. They talk for an hour. You learn: Hogtie, Ambush, Stalk. Your Codex overflows.
📢 SYSTEM CHALLENGE: "Catch something! Anything! We want to see how you do it!" (Hunt an animal today for a reward.)
✨ Ability gained: Lucky Rock (L1). Your lucky rock. The System finds your faith adorable and helps a little: +5% on the hunt. (It’s not the rock. It’s you believing in the rock.)
Overnight, tall sunflower-like stalks with knobby tubers at the base, found in sunny patches went bad — beyond saving. You leave it for the flies.
📨 Word came: a tired hunter of Thornfield wants to join Haven. "Word travels: Haven takes people in. I'm people." — they haven't set foot here. The village will judge.
"Tend the hurt, stretch the food, or hunt it back — pick one, maybe two, but everything costs something."
(Relief is open — triage, rations, hunt, or rally, from the beats row. Each option works once; the moment passes in ~3 days.)
You hunted at noon and at midnight in the same week, and neither darkness nor distance hid anything. The prey has filed a formal complaint about fairness.
Two eyes, forward-facing, unblinking. No wingsound. Owls don't make sound when they hunt — that's the problem.
"We can bind the wounds, or go lean, or hunt hard to replace what we lost. Say which — standing here isn't an answer."
